task: Focused RepoWise repair 003: OAuth draft recovery complexity review
metric_method: Read-only installed RepoWise walker and tree-sitter AST. No index recomputation or write.

behavior_and_order_evidence.verified: Read raw draft first; missing/empty raw value returns false without mutation. Invalid JSON, non-string text, and non-string provided identity/genre fields go through the recovery-preserving outer catch.

Already-restored comparison short-circuits in text/student/manual-genre/select-genre order. It allows a removal retry only for the same complete context; whitespace current writing remains occupied. Fallback precedence for select genre is explicit select value, manual value, then __auto__.
Text is written before selectedStudent. Optional localStorage selection hint failure is swallowed intentionally; failure must not block restoration or consume the wrong draft.
Missing student option is synthesized only in the select, with textContent, never added to the students roster. Missing select is tolerated; existing options are reused.
Manual genre and genre select follow student restoration, preserving distinct fallback expressions. syncUiState executes only after the complete field update.

Exact writing verification precedes raw-draft removal. Removal failure leaves restored UI and original bytes available for a coherent retry. A success notice follows removal and only applies to nonblank text.
Required read, parse, DOM, sync, verification or removal failure reports recovery error and returns false without deleting raw draft bytes.

The sole production caller is the window load handler. It clears the fresh text field, restores the OAuth draft, then initializes pending portfolio work, sync UI and Google session/redirect completion in that order.

The paired save function refuses unsafe redirects for tab-only pending work/photos and preserves an incompatible previous draft. It writes exactly the fields consumed here and does not offer a reusable DOM restore helper.
syncUiState may clear stale analysis and update feedback, image/genre controls and sync buttons. Moving it before full restoration would expose a different input context.

alternatives_considered: Extract draft validation and already-restored comparison: adds single-use predicates while retaining all schema/default/identity decisions; no caller reuse or duplicate validation to remove.
Extract student/genre restoration: removes the recovery mutation ordering from a short top-level transaction; still needs the same globals, optional storage catch and DOM branches.
Replace current comparisons/defaults with normalization, bulk assignment or a loop: changes or obscures value precedence, short-circuit reads, mutation order or missing-field behavior.
Drop the optional hint catch, strict raw validation, occupancy guard or post-sync exact-text check: changes the established recovery contract and was rejected.

findings.reason: CCN 29 is accurate: 10 if statements, two catches, seven && and nine || operators plus the entry path. The function is 45 nonblank lines, has no loops or awaits, and implements one synchronous recovery transaction. Validation and exact four-field identity checks protect malformed draft bytes and prevent replacing occupied writing; selection recovery keeps the chosen student represented without restoring a deleted roster; the inner catch makes a selection hint optional while the outer catch preserves required recovery failures. Draft removal follows UI restoration and exact text verification. Most comparisons/defaults cannot be removed without changing accepted data, conflict rules or error behavior. A split into one-use schema, identity and field-update helpers would move checks away from this short transaction and add call/closure boundaries without eliminating decisions or duplication. No existing helper performs this OAuth-specific operation. Retain the coherent transaction rather than introduce a score-only decomposition.
